limitations: A dead writer's committed tail can stay local: the ledger holds it, the drain counts it as pending with its damaged bytes and warns on its age, and no probe runs on every orphan pass (Codex Checkpoint C pass 1 ruling; ADR-032).

Diagnostic copy clock skew: a segment dated in the future by a clock that runs ahead stays selected until the date catches up; it is still rolled at 64 MiB and every record keeps its own time (Codex Checkpoint C pass 3).
The diagnostic copy is best effort and flushed, not fsynced; it is not an accounting boundary.
No claim of hardware power-loss survival, provider billing correctness or a generally working Phase 1 agent.
